title: Delete my account can be undone by a copy that was already sending
what: When a member taps Delete my account while the background copy is still sending (for example right after opening the app, or during a first copy of a long history), the copy keeps sending its remaining batches after the server has deleted the saved workouts. For an account that is also a gym owner's, trainer's or older gym-sync member's sign-in, the server keeps the sign-in, so those batches are saved again. The member is told the copy was deleted, but part or all of it is back on our server.
expected: Delete my account first stops and waits for any running copy, then deletes, so nothing is saved after the delete.
who: members whose sign-in is also a gym owner, trainer or older gym-sync account
how_often: rare: only when a copy is sending at the moment of the delete
fix_line: Pause the background copy and wait for it to finish before asking the server to delete, and stop it for good before saying done

title: Saved changes can wait up to 6 hours after the internet comes back
what: Each failed send makes the next try wait longer: 30 seconds, then 2, 8 and 32 minutes, about 2 hours, then 6 hours. A member who opens the app several times with no signal (a basement gym) builds up a long wait. When the internet returns, the app tries to send but skips everything whose wait has not run out, so the backup line keeps saying changes are waiting for hours on a working connection. The phone test of this case only checks a 30-second wait.
expected: When the internet comes back, or the member opens the app online, the waiting changes are sent at once.
who: signed-in members who train with weak or no signal
how_often: often for members in gyms with poor signal
fix_line: When the internet comes back, reset the wait on items that failed only for lack of internet

title: A server outage or server fault is shown to the member as no internet
what: Any server answer the copy does not recognise (the server down, overloaded, a timeout, a fault in the saving step) is treated the same as having no internet. The member reads that changes are waiting for the internet and a failed bring-back says to check the internet, while their connection is fine, and the waits grow as if offline.
expected: A server fault is told apart from no internet: the member reads that MettleUp's server is having trouble and nothing is lost, and the app tries again sooner.
who: every signed-in member during a server outage
how_often: during every server outage or server fault
fix_line: Add a server-trouble kind of failure with its own words and a short wait

title: MettleUp is never told when members' workout copies stop saving
what: The app reports crashes to MettleUp, but a copy that fails without crashing is written only to the phone's own log, which nobody reads in a real app. A server change that breaks saving, a copy refused as full or too big, members needing to sign in again, or a bring-back that keeps failing all stay on the phone. Every member could have a stuck backup for weeks and MettleUp would learn of it only when someone loses a phone and complains.
expected: Repeated copy failures send a short note with no personal data (the kind of failure and the app version) to MettleUp's own error report, and a daily health line shows how many copies saved today.
who: every signed-in member, and MettleUp support
fix_line: Send stuck-copy failures to the same error report that crashes use, once per kind per day

title: If the coach comes back, a slow AI company leaves it waiting for ever
what: The coach's calls to Claude and OpenAI have no time limit. If the AI company hangs during an outage, the chat keeps waiting with no reply and no error. The coach is switched off today.
expected: A call that takes longer than about a minute is stopped and the member reads that the AI did not answer, with the offline coach offered.
who: members using their own AI key, once the coach is switched on
fix_line: Add a time limit to each coach call

title: MettleUp cannot see how often members save, restore or undo a backup
what: Account sign-ins and saved copies can be counted on the server, but saving a backup file, restoring one, undoing a restore, and how often a restore fails happen only on the phone and are never counted. Whether to keep the backup file, and whether restores work for real members, is decided blind.
expected: A count with no personal data of backup saves, restores, undos and restore failures per day.
fix_line: Count backup saves, restores and failures in the daily health line
